relevance_note: Case series of five children with HA20: "We identified five heterozygous variants in the TNFAIP3 gene among the five children".
method_note: Worked by hand from the paper; a short Python script (scratch only) assembled the JSON, cut table-row spans and checked every span verbatim. Table 1, Table 2 and Table 3 have patients as columns; Table 1/2 column headers are 'Patient 1'..'Patient 5'; Table 3 header row is 'variant site' with patient names in its first data row 'Characteristics'. Table 1 YES/NO cells were read as observed/excluded; '/' cells in Tables 2 and 3 are not reported. Table 1 'Arthritis NO' does not exclude the checklist item 'arthritis or arthralgia'. Elevated inflammatory markers, abdominal pain, diarrhea and low hemoglobin are from statements naming all five children (group-inferred); 'two of the five patients experienced intermittent bloody stool' names no one and was not used. Previously published people in scope: Table 3 columns 2 and 4 ('The case reported by Xue et al'), column 6 ('The case reported by Zhong et al') and that case's mother, the infant of reference (32) and the patient of Harumi et al. (no reference number printed, no variant printed, so no variant row; TNFAIP3 not named for that person). Out of scope: the 168-patient literature review (group level only), Chen's study, Xue et al. (44) CNV, Lin et al. (46). Contradictions: (1) Table 3 column 5 is headed 'Patient 3' but carries c.133C>T: p. R45X, which Table 1 and the text give to Patient 4; its feature values (oral, genital, skin NO) contradict Patient 3 in Table 1 and its treatment contradicts Patient 4 in Table 1, so column 5 was not used for anyone. (2) The MMACHC variants (c.349G>C: p.A117P, c.482G>A: p.R161Q) are attributed to patient 3 in the Abstract and Discussion but to patient 2 in the Figure 1 legend; attribution is contradictory, so no MMACHC variant rows. The Treatment section states patient 2 was diagnosed with methylmalonic aciduria and received hydroxocobalamin; recorded for Patient 2 as stated. (3) Patient 2 oral ulcers: Table 1 and Table 3 say NO, the Discussion says 'patient 2 had rash, gastrointestinal ulcers, and oral ulcers'; both feature rows emitted, checklist not reported. (4) For the Xue case with c.1243_1247delAAAAC, Table 3 gives ALT 165.6 and AST 172.9 (reference 0~40) while the text says Xue's patients with that mutation had 'no liver injury and negative autoantibodies'; the text refers to 'patients' plural and was not tied to the column, so neither liver nor autoantibody status was recorded for Table 3 column 4. Inheritance: study patients recorded de novo from 'All patients were de novo (they have all been tested to confirm their origin)'; the Xue cases are labelled 'de novo' in Table 3 without any statement of parental testing, so their inheritance is not reported; the ref (32) 'de novo microdeletion' likewise has no parental-testing statement. Variant type for Patients 1, 2 and 5 ('small indels') does not match an enum class and frameshift is not stated, so not reported. Transcript NM_006290.5 comes from the Table 1 note and was applied to Table 1 cDNA variants only. Ages at onset come from the Discussion's paired lists ('patients 2, 5 ... 6 months and 1 year 6 months'; 'patients 1, 4 ... five years and shortly after birth'). Patient 2 'no liver injury' was taken to exclude autoimmune hepatitis. Ethnicity 'Chinese' from 'five unrelated Chinese families'.
